Systemet är redan hårt ansträngt, sade vd Amin Nasser på konferensen Energy Intelligence Forum i London. articles.title: Utlyser nyval i Spanien efter bostadskrisen
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Utlyser nyval i Spanien efter bostadskrisen
articles.body_text: Utlyser nyval i Spanien efter bostadskrisen Spaniens premiärminister Pedro Sánchez utlyser nyval sedan hans regering inte fått igenom sina förslag om nya åtgärder för att lösa landets bostadskris. Nyvalet ska hållas den 29 november. Beslutet att utlysa nyval meddelas under ett tv-sänt tal på måndagsmorgonen. Bostadspaketet, i huvudsak bestående av två olika lagar, lades fram efter det att en 87-årig kvinna vräktes från sin lägenhet i Madrid – vilket har fått spanjorernas ilska över bostadskrisen att kulminera. Förslagen syftade till att fram till år 2030 stoppa vräkningar av utsatta personer, göra det svårare att spekulera i fastigheter, att försvåra korttidsuthyrningar ytterligare, samt att hyreskontrakt förlängs automatiskt.

articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Tjänstesektorn ökar takten
articles.body_text: Index tar tempen på svensk tjänstesektor. Arkivbild Aktiviteten i tjänstesektorn ökade i september, enligt inköpschefsindex (PMI) från Swedbank och Silf. Indexet steg till 57,4 i september, jämfört med reviderade 56,0 månaden före. Kompositindex för september, där även tillverkningsindustrin räknas in, steg till 57,6 jämfört med reviderade 56,1 i augusti. Det sammanvägda inköpschefsindexet för eurozonen låg kvar på samma nivå, 53,1, jämfört med föregående månad, enligt siffror från Bloomberg. Ett indextal över 50 indikerar tillväxt medan ett indextal under 50 innebär en nedgång.

articles.title: Euron pressas av oro för svaga statsfinanser
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Euron pressas av oro för svaga statsfinanser
articles.body_text: Euron pressas av oro för svaga statsfinanser Euron faller till en lägsta nivån på nästan ett och ett halvt år. Trycket nedåt kommer från oro på marknaden för svaga statsfinanser i stora euroländer. Men trots eurons fall blir det inga valutavinster för svenskar på väg söderut. Kronan hänger med nedåt mot dollarn. I tidig morgonhandel är euron nere på 1,12 dollar per euro. För att hitta en svagare eurokurs får man gå tillbaka till maj 2025. Förutom Frankrikes stora budgetunderskott, statsskuld och politisk instabilitet inför nästa års presidentval i landet – som har tryckt upp riskpremien på franska statsobligationer till de högsta nivåerna sedan eurokrisen 2011 – bidrar marknadsoro för skuldtyngda Spanien, som ser ut att gå mot extraval. Samtidigt hämtar dollarn styrka från förväntningar på höjningar av styrräntan från USA:s centralbank Federal Reserve (Fed).

I Asien är flera storbörser fortsatt stängda till följd av helgdagar. Tokyobörsen har däremot öppet och inleder veckan på plus. Oljepriset håller sig kvar över 100 dollar. articles.title: Publicistiska grunden för journalistik på TV4
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.title: Nobel Prize 2026 awarded for showing how nerve cells shape feelings
articles.summary: US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded for their work.
articles.body_text: US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their work in the field of optogenetics. Their research has helped scientists learn more about the workings of the mind, to better understand how the human brain works. The Nobel Committee praised the trio for laying the foundation of a new era in neuroscience and revealing the neural circuits behind "specific memories, feelings, and behaviours relevant for neurological and psychiatric disorders". In clinical medicine, researchers are using the method to try to restore sight in people with visual impairment. "Optogenetics has fundamentally altered our understanding of the brain," the Nobel Assembly said. "Every day brings new discoveries, helping to solve one of humanity's great mysteries: how our incredible brain works." The winners said it was "absolutely wonderful" to get the award, and that it was an honour to share the accolade with friends. The three men will also share the £900,000 (12 million Swedish kronor) prize money. Per Svenningsson, chair of the Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine, explained: "Optogenetics provides opportunities for mapping the brain in a way that we could once only dream of." Before, the inner workings behind feelings, behaviours and bodily functions were more of a mystery to scientists. Optogentics is a way to illuminate brain pathways, using a special protein borrowed from algae that scientists use to control cell electrical activity using light. In the early 2000s, Hegemann and Nagel discovered channelrhodopsin, the algal protein with unique properties.

articles.title: 'Not again': Arrest of US marine for murder reignites protests in Japan's Okinawa
articles.summary: For many locals on this island, the arrest has brought decades of frustration back to the fore.
articles.body_text: For many Okinawa locals, the arrest of a US soldier accused of robbing and killing a woman in a hotel room has reignited decades of frustration over crimes involving US military personnel there. "Honestly my first reaction was, 'Not again,'" 52-year-old longtime Okinawa resident Ai Sato told the BBC. "Nothing has changed since I was a child. How many times are we going to repeat the same thing, create more victims, cause their families to suffer, and ultimately, cause the people of Okinawa to grieve?" Akemi Oshiro, a 62-year-old Ginowan resident shared similar sentiments. "I know we shouldn't get used to terrible things like this, but because they keep happening, I've stopped being surprised," she told the BBC. Okinawa hosts the largest US military presence in Japan. It is home to several US military bases and tens of thousands of American troops. US Marine Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, was arrested by Japanese police on Sunday. Police say an investigation is underway and that Ballard is in Japanese custody because the alleged crime was unrelated to official military duties. Whether a US service member is acting in the performance of official duty or not can determine which country has primary jurisdiction. When Japan has jurisdiction, but the suspect is under US custody, they can retain custody until Japan brings charges. Ballard was assigned to III Marine Expeditionary Force and stationed at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma in Ginowan City. The Okinawa prefectural police say 39-year-old Anna Yagi was found dead early 3 October in a hotel room in Naha. Security footage allegedly shows a man believed to be the suspect entering the hotel with the woman and leaving alone with her belongings. Local media citing police have reported that Yagi appeared to have been strangled with a cord. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi registered an official protest with Washington. But residents like Sato feel that's far from enough.

articles.title: Imran Khan: Supporters of jailed ex-PM begin march in Pakistan
articles.summary: Thousands have taken to the streets after talks between authorities and Khan's party ended in deadlock.
articles.body_text: Thousands of supporters of Pakistan's jailed ex-prime minister Imran Khan have begun a march from the country's north-west as they call for his release. Concerns over the 74-year-old's health have grown louder in recent months. His family claims he has lost most of his vision in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action. The cricket star-turned-politician, who faces charges in more than 100 cases, was jailed for 17 years over corruption last year. Khan said all the cases against him are politically motivated. Even behind bars, he remains a force in Pakistani politics, and demonstrations in his support have led to deadly violence and crackdowns in the past. The march began on Sunday in Lakki Marwat, a city 275km (170 miles) from Islamabad, and was expected to resume on Monday after pausing for the night. Originally scheduled for last week, it was postponed to allow for talks between the government and Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party but the talks ended in deadlock. Khan, who faces charges ranging from leaking state secrets to selling state gifts, was first imprisoned in August 2023. His wife Bushra Bibi was jailed along with him last year. Sohail Afridi, chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province which is governed by the PTI, expects the march to make its way to a town about 80km west of the capital Islamabad by Thursday. "[By then] this movement will have reached every corner of the country and every square will have become a centre of activity," he said on Sunday, urging the people to "play an active role in the political process". While the march organisers have not announced that they were heading for Islamabad, authorities have stacked up shipping containers to block key access routes to the capital. The PTI said talks with government failed because authorities rejected the party's request for access to Khan so that its leaders could consult him on national and political issues. The party also said it had demanded that Khan be given an immediate medical examination and treatment.

articles.title: All passengers presumed dead after plane went missing off US coast
articles.summary: The aircraft lost communication with flight controllers after significantly dropping in altitude, according to flight data.
articles.body_text: Six people aboard a medical transport aircraft that went missing on Saturday while it was travelling from Bermuda to Boston are presumed dead, according to a statement from the flight's operator. On Sunday evening, the United States Coast Guard said it was ending its search for survivors off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island. "We must now face the heartbreaking reality that the four members of our Latitude team, our patient and the patient's family escort, who were aboard Heartbeat 104, are presumed to have died," Latitude Air Ambulance said in a statement shortly thereafter. "Our thoughts are first and foremost with their families, loved ones, friends, and colleagues." The Federal Aviation Administration lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 plane just after 01:00 local time (05:00 GMT) on Saturday morning. On Saturday evening, authorities located a "debris field" confirmed to be from the aircraft. The plane had departed from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at 23:40 local time on Friday night, according to flight data from FlightAware, and was due to land at Boston's Logan International at 01:30 EDT (05:30 GMT). Four Canadian nationals and two Bermudian nationals were onboard. "This is an unimaginable loss for our Latitude family and for everyone who loved the six people aboard Heartbeat 104," said Peter Byl, President of Latitude Air Ambulance, on Sunday evening. "Our focus now is on supporting their families, supporting our people and assisting the authorities. We will honour our colleagues by remembering the care, professionalism, and commitment they brought to their work every day." Latitude Air Ambulance is a Canadian company that provides international medical flights for patients returning home. Two pilots and two medical staff, both Canadian, had flown to Bermuda to collect a patient and their relative, Clarence Togeretz, director of flight operations at Latitude, told CBC News.

articles.title: Trump chooses top spy boss to run new AI taskforce
articles.summary: The US president said his national intelligence chief will lead the group as worries over AI grow.
articles.body_text: US President Donald Trump has named the director of national intelligence as the head of a new taskforce on AI which, he said, will coordinate government engagement with consumers, companies and "religious organizations". Jay Clayton will head a taskforce that has drawn criticism from the likes of Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren who has called for regulation of AI. Trump has rejected the idea of laws to control development of the technology despite a debate about the potential risks of AI and what it means for humanity. Last week, the president and the heads of major AI firms signed a "morally binding" document, making them responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology. Trump - who is unilaterally attempting to rebrand AI as "super intelligence" - wrote on social media: "The Super Intelligence Force will coordinate the Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies." As well as Clayton, a former chair of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Andrew Ferguson, head of the Federal Trade Commission, will be on the taskforce along with Emil Michael, undersecretary of defense for research and engineering. It will report directly to Trump and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Trump has pushed back against any kind of slowdown on AI development. He said the US is leading the race ahead of China, adding: "And, frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins." President Xi Jinping recently travelled to Washington for a state visit. Days later, Trump ruled out a joint venture between the US and China to develop AI. "If we do that, we're going to be giving a lot of secrets that we have that they [China] would want to have, or anybody else," he said. The announcement of the taskforce follows growing pressure from prominent figures in the industry, including executives of OpenAI and Anthropic, to tighten regulation of the technology. Trump first announced the taskforce in September, prompting Warren to state: "Congress cannot meet the pressing threat of AI by just forming another committee or continuing to have drawn-out discussions about it."

articles.title: The sexual abuse of disabled residents that shocked South Korea
articles.summary: The BBC spoke to one of three residents at a care home who were sexually assaulted by a staff member.
articles.body_text: "I was hurting inside, so I came to tell my story." These were Seo Mi-hyeon's first words to the police. Seo, who has an intellectual disability, struggles to form long sentences and can only communicate through brief words and gestures. But her memories of the abuse inflicted upon her were clear. She was one of three residents at a state-run care home in South Korea who were sexually assaulted by the home's director, in a case that has shocked the country and raised serious questions about state care for the disabled. Earlier this month, a court in Seoul sentenced the director - who has only been identified by his surname Kim - to 15 years in prison. Kim is appealing the conviction. The court had heard that some residents were made to call the director "Dad", which prosecutors said illustrated the unequal relationship between Kim and those in his care. The ruling came nearly two years after Seo, who is in her 40s, first disclosed the abuse to her mother. We have changed Seo's name and the names of another victim in this story to protect their identities. Seo first began living in Saekdongwon, a care home for the intellectually disabled, in 2016. The institute, located in the city of Incheon, is fully subsidised by the state and still houses some 33 residents, although it has been asked to close down in light of this case. According to Seo, the abuse began shortly after she began living there, with Kim visiting her at night or in the early hours of the morning to rape her. Speaking through her lawyer Ko Eun-young, Seo said there was no adult at the facility she could speak to about the abuse, adding that she felt that other staff members would not help her. The care home has not responded to this allegation.

articles.title: US removes all bombers from RAF Fairford back to home stations
articles.summary: No reason has been given for the withdrawal, but it follows a major incident last week when police were alerted to "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase.
articles.body_text: The US has withdrawn all of its bombers from RAF Fairford, the UK military base at the centre of an incident being investigated by counter-terror police. A statement from a Pentagon official confirmed on Sunday it had removed its bombers - thought to be about a dozen B-1s - from the base back to their home stations in America. US media reported a new threat led to the bombers being removed, which follows a major incident on 27 September when police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase. Five men were initially arrested on suspicion of terror offences and subsequently released on bail. A sixth man, a UK-Iranian national, was also later arrested and released on bail. Whitehall officials have confirmed that in relation to the threats they are currently dealing with "there is an ongoing high tempo of threat from Iran to the UK, and it's logical that US airbases would be pretty high on any targeting list". They have also not disputed the decision from Washington was in response to the incident at the airbase in Gloucestershire. The BBC has also been told it was a military rather than a political decision - taken at an operational level - and communicated from the US military to its British counterparts. The UK's Ministry of Defence has not commented. Tracking websites showed B-1 bombers flying out of RAF Fairford on Sunday. The New York Times reported US commanders had received new threats about an Iran-backed plot against RAF Fairford according to two US officials. The newspaper wrote the new information was part of the same threat warnings from three weeks ago, but officials acted quickly after specific details emerged in the past 24 hours. The planes reportedly took off while aerial refueling aircraft were still being scrambled to support their flights to the US.

articles.title: Brazil election goes to run-off as right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro wins first round
articles.summary: With neither candidate getting more than 50% of the vote, the election will go to a run-off on 25 October.
articles.body_text: Right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro has won the first round of Brazil's presidential election, beating left-wing President Lula da Silva, but falling short of an outright majority. There will be a run-off between the two candidates on 25 October. Bolsonaro is the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year prison sentence for masterminding a failed coup after losing the 2022 election. Sunday's vote was close, with President Lula polling slightly ahead during the campaign. With almost all of the votes counted, Bolsonaro has 47% to Lula's 45% of the vote. Bolsonaro's result exceeded expectations, meaning the second round now looks like his to lose, given some of the other candidates knocked out in the first round were right-wing alternatives. Bolsonaro's Liberal Party (PL) also had the most governors, senators and federal deputies elected in the results so far, meaning the party is expected to have the most influence in Congress. The majority of Latin America has now elected right-wing presidents, aligned to the Trump administration, and the run-off will determine whether Brazil – Latin America's largest country and economy – will follow suit. After casting his ballot, Lula, 80, warned the choice was between democracy and "barbarism". Bolsonaro, 45, said he wanted to "free the Brazilian people". Lula and Bolsonaro are the two biggest names in Brazilian politics, on the left and right, and this campaign has polarised Brazil yet again: with themes of sovereignty, crime, the economy and corruption being top concerns for voters. Lula is more popular in Brazil's poorer northeast, among low-income voters, Catholics, and women. He is seeking a fourth term in office, after being elected in 2002, 2006 and then a later non-consecutive term in 2022. In that election, he beat Jair Bolsonaro by less than 2% of the vote, the closest presidential election result in Brazil's history.

articles.title: Up to 500 schools close in France over student protests
articles.summary: Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" in some high schools after clashes between riot police and student protesters, France's education minister says.
articles.body_text: Up to 500 schools across France will be partially or totally closed on Monday after clashes between riot police and student protesters in recent days, the French education minister said on Sunday. Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" in some "400 to 500" high schools as security conditions "have not been fulfilled", Édouard Geffray said. He also said 24 schools had been "burned or ransacked" since the start of the protests. Thousands of students have been demonstrating over education standards and the protests, which started last week, have spread from Paris to other cities, including Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille. High school pupils and others have objected to a lack of teachers, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings. On Friday, French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said 735 of France's 3,700 schools had been affected "one way or another" by violent protests. The education minister warned the number of schools potentially affected on Monday could be comparable to Friday's figure but promised a "partial, progressive return to lessons". "There are activists - particularly from the far-left - who have infiltrated the high school student movement, hijacked it from the students themselves, and engaged in extreme violence," Édouard Geffray claimed. "Clearly, this poses a risk to both our staff and our students," he said. Geffray added that 78 staff members in education had been wounded, which he described as "something we have never seen before". On Friday 1,747 people were arrested, according to French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez. Over 5,000 people have been arrested altogether since the start of the movement, according the AFP news agency, with around 85% of them minors. Organisers of the protests have called for the demonstrations to continue on Tuesday after accusing the government of a lack of "concrete measures", according to AFP.

articles.title: Yemen government announces major operation to retake Houthi territory
articles.summary: The Yemeni president's announcement comes amid an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition.
articles.body_text: The head of Yemen's internationally recognised government has announced it will wage an all out war in an effort to take all territory held by the Houthis. It follows an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in recent days. The Iran-backed group said it had struck sites belonging to Saudi national oil company Aramco, in response to what it described as 50 Saudi-led coalition strikes in 12 hours. Saudi Arabia has yet to comment. The Yemeni government's fierce statement was expected after the Houthis' offensive last month, which saw them seize control of the country's Red Sea coastline, including the vital shipping lane of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. On Sunday, Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address: "Today, I announce the start of military operations to retake the remaining territory of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory." Yemen's capital, Sanaa, which has been held by the Houthis for more than a decade, has come under sustained attack as government forces try to weaken the group's military capabilities. Attacks on the Houthis have also spread across Yemen, including to the Saada region, the group's northern heartland. But security sources say the Iran-backed Houthis have continued to make gains. The frontline in Yemen remains focused around the key city of Taiz, which is still controlled by the internationally recognised government. On Sunday, the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking Taiz with Aden, the interim capital of the Yemeni government, AFP news agency reports. Citing three Yemeni military sources, AFP also reports that the Houthis now control the area and supply route, effectively encircling Taiz. "They've achieved the military objective of isolating Taiz from Aden, even if they haven't fully taken control of it," Farea Al-Muslimi, a research fellow at the Chatham House think tank, told AFP.

articles.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
articles.summary: Footage shows a drone hitting the Pivnichyi (Northern) Bridge as vehicles move across it, creating a large fireball.
articles.body_text: Major bridges in Kyiv have been hit by Russian drone strikes for four consecutive days, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital. Two people were injured when the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge was struck on Sunday morning for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier in the week. The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a surprise visit to Kyiv in a show of support against Russia's continuing full-scale invasion. Russia's military said it would be intensifying strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions. It earlier said it had hit the two bridges used to transfer Ukrainian troops. Video footage of Sunday's strike, verified by the BBC, shows cars moving on Pivnichnyi Bridge as a drone crashes into it before exploding, creating a ball of fire. A cloud of black smoke can be seen rising above the bridge. Other videos and pictures have emerged on social media showing a gaping hole in the middle of a traffic lane on the bridge. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people were injured in the latest Russian attack. He earlier said that the Pivnichnyi Bridge's roadway was hit. Kyiv's eight bridges across the wide Dnipro River link the western (right) and eastern (left) parts, and many of the capital's estimated three million residents rely heavily on the metro lines and trains to travel across the city. Some 500,000 vehicles use the bridges every day. The two struck bridges are still standing - but the damage and restrictions to traffic and public transport have caused gridlock in parts of the capital at times. "To get from the left bank to the right one and back - it's just hell," Kyiv resident Roman told the BBC on Sunday. Large numbers of commuters cross the river, especially on weekdays. Repair teams are working to fix the damage and officials say they are planning temporary pontoon bridges, ferry services and even a tunnel under the river to keep Kyiv connected.

articles.title: Ghana bans preaching on buses with jail terms for offenders
articles.summary: Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread.
articles.body_text: Before the morning rush begins, the sound of praise and worship fills the Neoplan bus station in Ghana's capital, Accra, as a group of Christians gather to prepare to evangelise on vehicles taking travellers across the country. Amid drumming and dancing, Boateng Bismark James leads 13 worshippers, nine men and four women, in prayer for drivers and passengers travelling to destinations across Ghana. Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread. On long-distance buses, pastors can often be seen - and heard - preaching the gospel. Sometimes they stand in the stairwell next to the driver, at others they walk up and down the aisle reading from the Bible and calling on sinners to repent at the tops of their voices. They do not stop even if the trip lasts for several hours. The faithful sometimes offer money to the preachers to support their endeavours. But a new law means this familiar practice could be coming to an end. Anyone found preaching in public service vehicles faces up to eight months in prison, a fine of up to $52 (£39) or both. The new regulation, passed by parliament in May, and which has started to be enforced in recent weeks, targets preaching and hawking on vehicles while they are in motion, classifying both as a nuisance and citing the safety and comfort of passengers. Boateng, a 61-year-old pastor at Gospel Light church, has been preaching on commercial vehicles leaving Neoplan station since 2023. "I preach on commercial vehicles because not everyone is able to go to church on Sunday. There are a lot of passengers who need our message of salvation to repent from their sins. We even heal the sick on some buses," he told the BBC in Twi, a local language. Wearing a clerical collared shirt, Boateng moves through rows of buses loading passengers before boarding one bound for Kumasi, Ghana's second-largest city.

articles.title: Why Canada is wargaming a (long shot) US invasion
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the military is running scenarios in the unlikely case the US invades Canada.
articles.body_text: Prime Minister Mark Carney admitted last week that he has prepared for a once-unthinkable scenario - a US invasion. Noting the risk was low and the likelihood highly improbable, he told the New York Times he had a responsibility to consider all possibilities as the US-Canada relationship is redefined under the Donald Trump presidency. "That's just risk management," Carney said. Trump's global tariffs and his often-repeated desire to make Canada the 51st state has led Canada to war game an attack by the Americans. In 2025, the US president said it was "highly unlikely" that the US would ever use force against Canada. Instead he said, he would continue to exert economic pressures to obtain political aims. "President Trump has done more than anyone to protect the great people of Canada," the White House told the BBC in a statement this week. Military experts who spoke to the BBC also think an invasion is a long shot, pointing to the multiple ways the two countries work together on defence. But the issue is clearly weighing on Canadians' minds. In January, after the US captured Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela, a Leger poll suggested that over 30% of Canadians believed that a US invasion was likely. A war between Canada and the US would be complicated and almost difficult to imagine, said Lt-Gen Christopher Coates, a former military officer of 34 years with the Royal Canadian Air Force who held various senior positions. "I was involved in military operations for my whole career, and we never considered the possibility that there would be a military attack coming from US territory," he told the BBC. Coates, who had served on Nato missions, noted that Canada and the US collaborate on many aspects of military defence.

articles.title: Perú vs. Colombia: ¿a qué hora juegan y dónde ver el amistoso de la fecha FIFA 2026?
articles.summary: La selección peruana enfrentará a Colombia este martes 6 de octubre en Miami, en un amistoso internacional correspondiente a la fecha FIFA.
articles.body_text: La selección peruana ya tiene todo listo para su último compromiso de la fecha FIFA de octubre. Perú vs. Colombia se medirán este martes 6 de octubre en Miami, en un encuentro que marcará el cierre de la gira norteamericana dirigida por Mano Menezes. El partido comenzará a las 6:45 p. m. (hora peruana) y podrá ser visto en territorio nacional a través de América TV, mientras que la cobertura digital también estará disponible mediante América tvGO. El amistoso entre Perú y Colombia está programado para las 6:45 p. m. en Perú y Colombia, mientras que en Miami el inicio será a las 7:45 p. m. En otros países de Sudamérica, el encuentro comenzará a las 8:45 p. m. en Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Paraguay y Uruguay. El escenario será el Nu Stadium de Miami, recinto con capacidad para más de 26.000 espectadores. Para los hinchas que quieran seguir el encuentro desde Perú, la transmisión estará a cargo de América TV. La señal también anunció que llevará los amistosos de la Bicolor durante esta fecha FIFA a través de sus plataformas. En consecuencia, el duelo ante Colombia podrá seguirse por televisión y mediante las opciones digitales habilitadas por América Multimedia. La Bicolor llegará al compromiso con la necesidad de cerrar la gira con una actuación positiva. Perú perdió 4-1 ante Estados Unidos, empató 1-1 frente a México y posteriormente cayó 2-0 contra Canadá. El encuentro ante Colombia será, por ello, el cuarto y último partido de esta serie de amistosos internacionales antes de los compromisos programados para noviembre. Colombia tampoco llega después de una victoria. El conjunto dirigido por Néstor Lorenzo empató 1-1 con México el 26 de septiembre y perdió 1-0 frente a Paraguay el 2 de octubre. La Federación Colombiana de Fútbol confirmó que el duelo contra Perú será el cierre de su participación en esta fecha FIFA, también como parte de su proceso de preparación para los próximos desafíos internacionales. Más allá del resultado, el amistoso tendrá especial importancia para el proceso de Mano Menezes. La selección peruana atraviesa una etapa de renovación y estos partidos permiten al comando técnico evaluar jugadores, probar variantes y encontrar una base para los siguientes desafíos. El duelo ante Colombia será además la última presentación de la Bicolor en esta fecha FIFA de septiembre-octubre. El partido también servirá como una nueva oportunidad para que Perú encuentre respuestas después de sus tres primeros encuentros de la gira. Colombia, por su parte, buscará cerrar su calendario con un triunfo después de sus resultados ante México y Paraguay. Con ambos equipos en procesos de preparación, el encuentro en Miami aparece como una prueba más dentro del camino hacia las próximas competiciones oficiales.

articles.title: Miraflores: incendio en parque de Malecón de la Reserva afecta geomallas
articles.summary: Miraflores: incendio en Malecón de la Reserva afecta geomallas
articles.body_text: Un incendio se reporta en el parque Domodossola, en Malecón de la Reserva, distrito de Miraflores. El siniestro ocurrió al promediar las 9 de la mañana. Al lugar llegaron 16 unidades del Cuerpo de los Bomberos del Perú para atender la emergencia que causa preocupación entre los asistentes a dicha zona. Mario Casaretto, gerente de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres de la Municipalidad Metropolitana de Lima (MML), indicó que parte de las geomallas utilizadas para evitar desprendimiento de rocas y plantas, han sido afectadas. Las llamas están cerca al centro comercial Larcomar y exactamente a 70 metros el recientemente inaugurado teleférico de Miraflores. Según testigos del siniestro, un grupo de turistas que paseaba por la zona fueron llevados nuevamente a su hotel para no ser afectados por el humo. También, algunas personas que en ese momento se encontraban en el Colegio Médico del Perú para votar por las Elecciones Regionales y Municipales 2026, fueron cubiertas por cenizas. Personal de Serenazgo y la Policía Nacional del Perú (PNP), han cerrado esta vía en ambas direcciones. En tanto, los bomberos continúan realizando trabajos denodados para controlar el incendio y llegar hasta la zona donde se habría iniciado el fuego, sin embargo, el acceso al acantilado dificulta el acceso a las mangueras. Minutos más tarde de haberse producido el incendio, se reportó una persona herida. articles.body_text: El candidato a primer regidor de la Municipalidad de Lima por Renovación Popular, Rafael López Aliaga, defendió su postulación y la posibilidad que pueda asumir como nuevo burgomaestre en el próximo periodo. El dirigente político sostuvo que su inscripción respetó las normas vigentes en la legislación electoral y que, tal como está la norma, podría incluso volver a postular en el 2030. “De acuerdo a la ley, en este minuto, hoy día yo podría ir hasta un tercer periodo. No es mi intención, pero podría”, declaró el postulante en una entrevista con RPP este viernes. El aspirante edil explicó que dicha opción legal derivó de su postulación como teniente alcalde y no como alcalde titular. López Aliaga precisó que la prohibición de reelección inmediata se refiere de forma exclusiva al cargo de alcalde. El candidato recordó que el Jurado Nacional de Elecciones respaldó la validez de su lista partidaria de manera definitiva en fallos recientes. “El verbo que se debe aplicar acá es postular, no estoy postulando a alcalde, estoy postulando a teniente alcalde, y por ausencia del titular me toca asumir”, afirmó el aspirante. El dirigente reiteró que su candidatura cumplió con los requisitos legales establecidos para el proceso edil. López Aliaga señaló que la normativa vigente prevé la entrega de la credencial de alcalde al primer regidor en caso de victoria de su partido. El postulante indicó que asumirá la conducción de Lima si Renovación Popular logra el triunfo en las elecciones del 4 de octubre. “Mi opinión personal, te digo que un alcalde sí debería tener una reelección, una reelección inmediata para poder terminar. Cuatro años es muy poco”, expresó el líder político. El candidato argumentó que las gestiones municipales requieren mayor tiempo para la ejecución de obras de infraestructura en la capital. “Este miércoles voy a declarar como acusador a toda la mafia criminal de ONPE y voy a meterlos a la cárcel 20 años por haber robado la voluntad popular”, sostuvo el dirigente. El candidato denunció supuestas irregularidades cometidas por las autoridades electorales durante los comicios anteriores del 2026 cuando buscó ser presidente de la República. López Aliaga, en otro momento, cuestionó la imparcialidad del Jurado Nacional de Elecciones en la resolución de las tachas presentadas contra postulantes. Por esto, confirmó la presencia de personeros en todas las mesas de votación para la vigilancia del escrutinio en la capital.

articles.body_text: La selección peruana ya tiene todo listo para su último compromiso de la fecha FIFA de octubre. (hora peruana) y podrá ser visto en territorio nacional a través de América TV, mientras que la cobertura digital también estará disponible mediante América tvGO. El amistoso entre Perú y Colombia está programado para las 6:45 p. m. en Perú y Colombia, mientras que en Miami el inicio será a las 7:45 p. m. En otros países de Sudamérica, el encuentro comenzará a las 8:45 p. m. en Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Paraguay y Uruguay. El escenario será el Nu Stadium de Miami, recinto con capacidad para más de 26.000 espectadores. Para los hinchas que quieran seguir el encuentro desde Perú, la transmisión estará a cargo de América TV. La señal también anunció que llevará los amistosos de la Bicolor durante esta fecha FIFA a través de sus plataformas. En consecuencia, el duelo ante Colombia podrá seguirse por televisión y mediante las opciones digitales habilitadas por América Multimedia. La Bicolor llegará al compromiso con la necesidad de cerrar la gira con una actuación positiva. Más allá del resultado, el amistoso tendrá especial importancia para el proceso de Mano Menezes. La selección peruana atraviesa una etapa de renovación y estos partidos permiten al comando técnico evaluar jugadores, probar variantes y encontrar una base para los siguientes desafíos. El duelo ante Colombia será además la última presentación de la Bicolor en esta fecha FIFA de septiembre-octubre. El partido también servirá como una nueva oportunidad para que Perú encuentre respuestas después de sus tres primeros encuentros de la gira. articles.title: El dólar cierra en S/3,43 tras débil reporte de empleo en Estados Unidos
articles.summary: El precio del dólar cerró este viernes 2 de octubre en S/3,436, con una caída de 0,5% frente a los S/3,453 de la jornada anterior.
articles.body_text: El precio del dólar cerró este viernes 2 de octubre en S/3,436, con una caída de 0,5% frente a los S/3,453 de la jornada anterior. El retroceso se produjo luego de que el reporte de empleo de Estados Unidos mostrará una creación de puestos de trabajo significativamente menor a la esperada, reduciendo las expectativas de una nueva subida de tasas de la Reserva Federal (Fed) en octubre. “Las nóminas no agrícolas aumentaron en apenas 29 mil durante septiembre, frente a las 90 mil esperadas, mientras que la tasa de desempleo subió a 4,2%. Tras conocerse estos resultados, la probabilidad de una subida de tasas de la Fed en octubre se redujo a 21%, desde 26% antes del dato”, explicó Jorge Luis Huayta, trader FX de Kambista. En ese contexto, el Índice del Dólar Estadounidense (DXY) retrocedió 0,09%, mientras que el rendimiento del bono del Tesoro a 10 años llegó a 5,34%, máximo desde 2002. La corrección del dólar favoreció a varias monedas internacionales y de la región. El peso colombiano avanzó 1,35%, el peso mexicano 0,50% y el real brasileño 0,10%, mientras que el peso chileno retrocedió 0,49%. Las materias primas, en cambio, registraron caídas: el petróleo WTI cedió 1,06%, el oro 0,94%, la plata 1,07%, el cobre 0,22% y el zinc 1,40%. En el mercado local, el USD/PEN pasó de S/3,453 a S/3,434, acumulando una apreciación del sol de 1,9 céntimos. Durante la jornada, el tipo de cambio fluctuó entre S/3,430 y S/3,442, con un volumen negociado de US$597.5 millones. El mercado había iniciado la sesión alrededor de S/3,440, mientras los agentes asimilaban el reporte laboral estadounidense. Asimismo, el BCR dejó vencer un swap cambiario compra por S/400 millones, ejerciendo una oferta indirecta en el mercado cambiario. “De cara a la próxima semana, la atención estará puesta en la decisión de política monetaria del BCRP del jueves. El mercado espera que la tasa de referencia se mantenga en 4,25% y los últimos datos de inflación serán relevantes para esta decisión”, agregó Huayta. En el ámbito local, también se mantiene entre los principales riesgos la posibilidad de un Fenómeno El Niño extraordinario, de acuerdo con las advertencias señaladas por especialistas. Jimena Torres, gerente de intermediación de Divisas en Renta4 SAB, agregó que hoy se negociaron 597 millones en el mercado spot interbancario, 19% más del flujo visto ayer (499 millones). El PMI manufacturero de EE.UU. subió a 55.9 puntos en septiembre, desde 53.9, pero quedó por debajo de los 57.0 esperados. La lectura sigue mostrando una expansión sólida de la actividad industrial, aunque con menor dinamismo del previsto por el mercado.

articles.summary: La selección peruana enfrentará a Colombia este martes 6 de octubre en Miami, en un amistoso internacional correspondiente a la fecha FIFA.
articles.body_text: La selección peruana ya tiene todo listo para su último compromiso de la fecha FIFA de octubre. Perú vs. Colombia se medirán este martes 6 de octubre en Miami, en un encuentro que marcará el cierre de la gira norteamericana dirigida por Mano Menezes. El partido comenzará a las 6:45 p. m. (hora peruana) y podrá ser visto en territorio nacional a través de América TV, mientras que la cobertura digital también estará disponible mediante América tvGO. El amistoso entre Perú y Colombia está programado para las 6:45 p. m. en Perú y Colombia, mientras que en Miami el inicio será a las 7:45 p. m. En otros países de Sudamérica, el encuentro comenzará a las 8:45 p. m. en Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Paraguay y Uruguay. El escenario será el Nu Stadium de Miami, recinto con capacidad para más de 26.000 espectadores. Para los hinchas que quieran seguir el encuentro desde Perú, la transmisión estará a cargo de América TV. La señal también anunció que llevará los amistosos de la Bicolor durante esta fecha FIFA a través de sus plataformas. En consecuencia, el duelo ante Colombia podrá seguirse por televisión y mediante las opciones digitales habilitadas por América Multimedia. La Bicolor llegará al compromiso con la necesidad de cerrar la gira con una actuación positiva. Perú perdió 4-1 ante Estados Unidos, empató 1-1 frente a México y posteriormente cayó 2-0 contra Canadá. El encuentro ante Colombia será, por ello, el cuarto y último partido de esta serie de amistosos internacionales antes de los compromisos programados para noviembre. Más allá del resultado, el amistoso tendrá especial importancia para el proceso de Mano Menezes. La selección peruana atraviesa una etapa de renovación y estos partidos permiten al comando técnico evaluar jugadores, probar variantes y encontrar una base para los siguientes desafíos. El duelo ante Colombia será además la última presentación de la Bicolor en esta fecha FIFA de septiembre-octubre. El partido también servirá como una nueva oportunidad para que Perú encuentre respuestas después de sus tres primeros encuentros de la gira. Colombia, por su parte, buscará cerrar su calendario con un triunfo después de sus resultados ante México y Paraguay. Con ambos equipos en procesos de preparación, el encuentro en Miami aparece como una prueba más dentro del camino hacia las próximas competiciones oficiales.

Personal de Serenazgo y la Policía Nacional del Perú (PNP), han cerrado esta vía en ambas direcciones. En tanto, los bomberos continúan realizando trabajos denodados para controlar el incendio y llegar hasta la zona donde se habría iniciado el fuego, sin embargo, el acceso al acantilado dificulta el acceso a las mangueras. Minutos más tarde de haberse producido el incendio, se reportó una persona herida. Canal N indicó que esta recibió atención en el lugar por parte de efectivos de la Policía Nacional del Perú (PNP), y personas que se encontraban en la zona. articles.title: China Polo: dictan 18 meses de prisión preventiva contra investigados por su asesinato
articles.summary: El Juzgado Penal de Investigación Preparatoria de Huaylas-Caraz dictó 18 meses de prisión preventiva contra dos investigados de nacionalidad venezolana por el asesinato de Susy Aponte Polo, conocida como China Polo. La resolución judicial incluye cargos por sicariato y lesiones graves contra cuatro ciudadanos que sufrieron disparos de arma de fuego durante el ataque.
articles.body_text: El Juzgado Penal de Investigación Preparatoria de Huaylas-Caraz dictó 18 meses de prisión preventiva contra dos investigados de nacionalidad venezolana por el asesinato de Susy Aponte Polo, conocida como China Polo. La resolución judicial incluye cargos por sicariato y lesiones graves contra cuatro ciudadanos que sufrieron disparos de arma de fuego durante el ataque. El Poder Judicial ordenó el internamiento penal de Luis Iván Obispo Díaz en calidad de autor directo del homicidio por encargo cometido en Huaylas. La Fiscalía le atribuye un pago de S/15,000 por ejecutar el disparo directo contra la postulante a la gobernación regional. La medida judicial comprendió además a Ronald José Toro Ardila como presunto financista y cómplice primario de la operación criminal. El Ministerio Público acreditó transferencias digitales desde su cuenta bancaria para pagar el hospedaje, los traslados y la compra del teléfono celular usado en el hecho. La Fiscalía sostuvo que ambos procesados carecen de arraigo domiciliario en el país y representan un peligro de fuga extremo. Las pericias balísticas, los testimonios presenciales y las inspecciones técnicas reforzaron los elementos de convicción aceptados por el juzgado. El juez dispuso el traslado de los imputados a un penal mientras continúan las diligencias de la investigación preparatoria. Las autoridades buscan determinar la identidad de los autores intelectuales que ordenaron el crimen de la candidata regional. El sicario atacó a disparos a China Polo el 19 de septiembre en las inmediaciones del mercado central de la ciudad de Caraz, en Áncash. La víctima realizaba una caminata proselitista junto a simpatizantes de su agrupación política cuando recibió el impacto directo en la cabeza. El atacante al usar su arma de fuego contra Aponte hirió a transeúntes y comensales en el lugar del suceso. Una mujer de 72 años perdió la vida doce días después debido a las graves heridas causadas por los proyectiles. Efectivos de la Policía Nacional capturaron a Obispo Díaz en la escena del crimen en posesión de una pistola tras un enfrentamiento armado. Las fuerzas del orden detuvieron posteriormente a Toro Ardila en Lima mediante un operativo de rastreo de sus cuentas bancarias.

articles.title: Perú vs. Colombia: ¿a qué hora juegan y dónde ver el amistoso de la fecha FIFA 2026?
articles.summary: La selección peruana enfrentará a Colombia este martes 6 de octubre en Miami, en un amistoso internacional correspondiente a la fecha FIFA.
articles.body_text: La selección peruana ya tiene todo listo para su último compromiso de la fecha FIFA de octubre. Perú vs. Colombia se medirán este martes 6 de octubre en Miami, en un encuentro que marcará el cierre de la gira norteamericana dirigida por Mano Menezes. El partido comenzará a las 6:45 p. m. (hora peruana) y podrá ser visto en territorio nacional a través de América TV, mientras que la cobertura digital también estará disponible mediante América tvGO. El amistoso entre Perú y Colombia está programado para las 6:45 p. m. en Perú y Colombia, mientras que en Miami el inicio será a las 7:45 p. m. En otros países de Sudamérica, el encuentro comenzará a las 8:45 p. m. en Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Paraguay y Uruguay. El escenario será el Nu Stadium de Miami, recinto con capacidad para más de 26.000 espectadores. Para los hinchas que quieran seguir el encuentro desde Perú, la transmisión estará a cargo de América TV. La señal también anunció que llevará los amistosos de la Bicolor durante esta fecha FIFA a través de sus plataformas. En consecuencia, el duelo ante Colombia podrá seguirse por televisión y mediante las opciones digitales habilitadas por América Multimedia. La Bicolor llegará al compromiso con la necesidad de cerrar la gira con una actuación positiva. Perú perdió 4-1 ante Estados Unidos, empató 1-1 frente a México y posteriormente cayó 2-0 contra Canadá. El encuentro ante Colombia será, por ello, el cuarto y último partido de esta serie de amistosos internacionales antes de los compromisos programados para noviembre. Colombia tampoco llega después de una victoria. El conjunto dirigido por Néstor Lorenzo empató 1-1 con México el 26 de septiembre y perdió 1-0 frente a Paraguay el 2 de octubre. La Federación Colombiana de Fútbol confirmó que el duelo contra Perú será el cierre de su participación en esta fecha FIFA, también como parte de su proceso de preparación para los próximos desafíos internacionales. Más allá del resultado, el amistoso tendrá especial importancia para el proceso de Mano Menezes. La selección peruana atraviesa una etapa de renovación y estos partidos permiten al comando técnico evaluar jugadores, probar variantes y encontrar una base para los siguientes desafíos. El duelo ante Colombia será además la última presentación de la Bicolor en esta fecha FIFA de septiembre-octubre. El partido también servirá como una nueva oportunidad para que Perú encuentre respuestas después de sus tres primeros encuentros de la gira. Colombia, por su parte, buscará cerrar su calendario con un triunfo después de sus resultados ante México y Paraguay. Con ambos equipos en procesos de preparación, el encuentro en Miami aparece como una prueba más dentro del camino hacia las próximas competiciones oficiales.

articles.body_text: Un incendio se reporta en el parque Domodossola, en Malecón de la Reserva, distrito de Miraflores. El siniestro ocurrió al promediar las 9 de la mañana. Al lugar llegaron 16 unidades del Cuerpo de los Bomberos del Perú para atender la emergencia que causa preocupación entre los asistentes a dicha zona. Mario Casaretto, gerente de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres de la Municipalidad Metropolitana de Lima (MML), indicó que parte de las geomallas utilizadas para evitar desprendimiento de rocas y plantas, han sido afectadas. Las llamas están cerca al centro comercial Larcomar y exactamente a 70 metros el recientemente inaugurado teleférico de Miraflores. Según testigos del siniestro, un grupo de turistas que paseaba por la zona fueron llevados nuevamente a su hotel para no ser afectados por el humo. También, algunas personas que en ese momento se encontraban en el Colegio Médico del Perú para votar por las Elecciones Regionales y Municipales 2026, fueron cubiertas por cenizas. Personal de Serenazgo y la Policía Nacional del Perú (PNP), han cerrado esta vía en ambas direcciones. En tanto, los bomberos continúan realizando trabajos denodados para controlar el incendio y llegar hasta la zona donde se habría iniciado el fuego, sin embargo, el acceso al acantilado dificulta el acceso a las mangueras. Minutos más tarde de haberse producido el incendio, se reportó una persona herida. Canal N indicó que esta recibió atención en el lugar por parte de efectivos de la Policía Nacional del Perú (PNP), y personas que se encontraban en la zona. De acuerdo con información preliminar, se trataría aparentemente de una persona en situación de calle.

El candidato argumentó que las gestiones municipales requieren mayor tiempo para la ejecución de obras de infraestructura en la capital. “Este miércoles voy a declarar como acusador a toda la mafia criminal de ONPE y voy a meterlos a la cárcel 20 años por haber robado la voluntad popular”, sostuvo el dirigente. articles.title: Can ‘super intelligence’ and a non-binding safety pact solve AI’s image problem? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: On Equity, we discussed the Trump administration's attempts to rebrand AI.
articles.body_text: President Donald Trump hosted many of the biggest names in artificial intelligence this week — in part to announce that the U.S. government isn’t calling it artificial intelligence anymore. Now it’s super intelligence. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed the motivation behind the meeting and what effect it might have on the AI industry. We were all pretty skeptical that the “Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities” that the executives signed will amount to much, especially since — as Sean noted — it’s “deeply non-binding,” at least from a legal prospective. (Instead, Trump said he considers it “morally binding.”) Kirsten suggested that the meeting’s real significance may have been as “a rebranding effort around AI.” (An effort that continued this weekend with Trump’s announcement of a new Super Intelligence Force .) For her, the big message was, “AI is going to kill us, it’s scary, it is going to take jobs — but super intelligence is not.” Keep reading for a preview of our conversation , edited for length and clarity. Anthony Ha: Officially, by order of the president of the United States, it’s not artificial intelligence anymore, it’s super intelligence. We were talking about this last week , because this is something [Trump has] been hinting at — he doesn’t do hints, he’s been saying [it] for a while. But now it’s signed into executive order. If you’re an official U.S. representative, you are supposed to say super intelligence, not artificial intelligence. And this was also part of this broader announcement around AI safety, which I think is both interesting for this pact that was announced, but also the fact that it happened at all. It seemed to have come together fairly quickly, because just two weeks ago, a week ago, President Trump was saying, “We don’t need any of this, we need to lead in AI, we can’t constrain it in any way, we don’t need any regulation, anyone who’s saying that there’s any danger from AI is essentially a Chinese or Democratic plant.” And yet all these AI CEOs got together with him earlier this week and signed this pact. Kirsten Korosec: Leading up to that, we should say, not only was there pushback on regulation, and we can talk about whether this executive order even does any of that — I would say no, there’s a little bit of theater there — but the important and interesting thing is that just days ago, Anthropic was really in the doghouse, if you will, in terms of what was happening behind the scenes with President Trump. That all changed when [Anthropic CEO] Dario Amodei was invited to a 10 p.m. dinner. He had this sit-down, and then just days later, we had this luncheon, and at this luncheon, we have pretty much every tech power broker from every major tech company that exists. So Mark Zuckerberg was there, Jeff Bezos was there, Elon Musk was there, Dario of course was there, they were all there. I’m wondering if any of you watched the press conference that happened afterwards, which there’s been many, many memes about, because of the interesting, funny behavior when you bring a bunch of tech CEOs together. But I guess my bigger question for both of you is: What does this all mean? And does it mean anything? Sean O’Kane: How much time do you have? First off, sure, they had dinner, Trump and Dario. If you read the Time magazine interview that Trump just did, your guess is as good as mine as to how informed he was that that dinner was even going to be happening, which is a strange reality to live in, but it’s just the one we inhabit. I will also say one other thing that makes me skeptical — surprise, surprise — of how repaired the relationship is between the administration and Anthropic, is that for as much as there are clearly people trying to put those two groups together, the Defense Department is still very adamant that Anthropic is terrible and woke and and a national security risk. Emil Michael goes off on Anthropic every other day on X, it seems. I think there’s still some distance there despite Dario showing up to this thing.

articles.title: TechCrunch Mobility: Reining in robotaxis | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.
articles.body_text: On an average day in San Francisco, you might see dozens (hundreds?) of Waymo robotaxis zipping around the city — and with little disruption. But, as TechCrunch has reported, there have been numerous incidents of robotaxis impeding traffic, driving into crime scenes, and interfering with first responders. And not just in the Bay Area. In some cases, companies have relied on first responders to move their robotaxis. These disruptions are occurring in the early stages of the robotaxi era. California has a new law hoping to get ahead of the problem before the next impending wave of robotaxis land. Senate Bill 1246, which was signed into law by Governor Gavin Newsom this week, sets a series of new rules for AVs designed to improve safety and response times when they become disabled or interfere with emergency responders. The law also creates ways to hold these companies accountable if they don’t. Autonomous vehicle technology companies like Tesla , Waymo , and Zoox will have to provide first responders with local, on-the-ground support when their robotaxis cause problems and could also face penalties if a robotaxi blocks police or firefighters for more than 30 minutes. The law also says AV developers can only employ remote drivers who are based in the United States and those drivers must hold a U.S. driver’s license. They must also notify cities, towns, and other local jurisdictions about the location and status of vehicles during system-wide failures and must provide “local incident technicians” who can assist with AV accidents and obstructions. There are still some details to hammer out, which the Department of Motor Vehicles will handle since it’s the main regulator of autonomous vehicles in the state. But when this law goes into effect in July 2028, will it actually keep robotaxis out of the way of emergency responders? It likely won’t, but hopefully this law reduces the chaos and raises the accountability when something does happen. Perhaps the better question is will other states follow California’s lead or wait for the federal government to weigh in? Harbinger , the EV startup, landed a $300 million deal to supply FedEx with 2,000 of its electric trucks. HyperGuest , an Israeli travel tech startup, raised $25 million from AMI, the investment arm of Apax Partners. REGENT Craft , the developer and manufacturer of the all-electric Seaglider, extended its collaboration with the U.S. Marine Corps Warfighting Lab, pushing the total value of the contract to $19.25 million. Quartermaster , an Arlington, Virginia-based maritime intelligence startup, raised $140 million in a Series B round. About $100 million came from Insight Partners, defense-focused firm Overmatch Ventures, and First Round Capital. The remaining $40 million came in the form of a debt facility from investment bank Stifel.

articles.title: Trump unveils his new Super Intelligence Force | TechCrunch
articles.summary: This new task force is Trump's latest response to the debate over AI safety.
articles.body_text: As promised, President Donald Trump has announced the formation of a new Super Intelligence Force, which he said will be led by national intelligence director Jay Clayton and other members of his administration. “The Super Intelligence Force is tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence, which many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet, and will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans,” Trump said in a Sunday morning post on his social network Truth Social. Back in September, in response to an AI safety debate that the president has largely dismissed as a hoax created by “Radical Left Dumocrats,” Trump said he would nevertheless form an AI Force and appoint an AI czar (“Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!”). Since then, Trump signed an executive order seeking to rebrand AI as “super intelligence,” a term seemingly embraced, with some stumbles , by the tech executives who gathered at the White House this week to sign a non-binding safety pledge. (The pledge included an impressive typo .) So it’s only natural that Trump’s new task force is named in accordance with this new branding. The Wall Street Journal reports that Clayton will chair the Super Intelligence Force, effectively making him the new AI/SI czar, with Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson, Undersecretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael, and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor serving as vice chairs. The task force will reportedly have 120 days to create a report on the risks and opportunities presented by AI. Clayton, who previously said that it would be irresponsible for the United States to “back away” from AI while countries like China advance, made similar comments to the WSJ, insisting that one of the biggest risks is “not being first.” The task force’s charter reportedly says that it will “develop plans for responding to SI-enabled threats to our society, while preventing overregulation and regulatory capture that would stifle innovation and competition.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Federal judge calls Flock ‘indiscriminate mass surveillance’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A federal judge ruled that a sheriff’s deputy violated a woman’s Fourth Amendment rights when using Flock to search for her license plate without a warrant.
articles.body_text: A federal judge ruled this week that a Tulsa, Oklahoma sheriff’s deputy violated a woman’s Fourth Amendment rights when using Flock Safety to search for her license plate without a warrant. As reported by 404 Media , this ruling does not create a binding precedent, but it is one of the first times that a federal judge has ruled that a Flock search is unconstitutional. In this case, Judge Sara Hill said the deputy should have obtained a warrant before searching the Flock database for the woman’s license plate, as he had “no apparent reason” for the search “other than the fact that [the woman’s vehicle] had a California license plate.” The deputy then used the woman’s travel history in Flock as part of the justification for searching her car, where he allegedly discovered 91 pounds of meth. But Judge Hill wrote that all evidence obtained after the Flock search “must be suppressed as the fruit of a poisonous tree.” Judge Hill also took broader aim at warrantless searches of the Flock database, writing that tracking people’s location — even when they’re in public places — becomes “constitutionally problematic when law enforcement can indiscriminately and passively catalog your whereabouts over an extended period of time and then use that information for any purpose whenever convenient.” “This is a type of indiscriminate mass surveillance,” Hill wrote. “It is not targeted on a single individual, as in [ Carpenter v. United States , a Supreme Court case focused on how government agencies access location data from cell phones ]. It is a tool that collects information about all vehicles that pass by any network-connected camera at all times, and it serves up the information to law enforcement on demand.” Hill joins a growing chorus of Flock critics from across the political spectrum. Numerous local and state governments, including Florida and Texas , have said they will stop using the technology. And on Friday, Senator Bernie Sanders introduced the Block Flock Act , which would bar federal agencies from using automated license plate readers such as Flock. articles.title: Amazon responds to data center backlash, says it no longer uses NDAs | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The CEO of Amazon Web Services tried to push back against widespread suspicion of data centers.
articles.body_text: Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman said the company has stopped using nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) in its dealings with government agencies as it seeks approval to build new data centers. Garman’s statement is just one sentence in a longer blog post in which he tried to push back against widespread suspicion of data centers, and to make the case that they’re actually good for communities. NDAs are a significant piece of the broader data center backlash. For example, environmental activist Erin Brockovich recently said that the number one complaint she’s heard about data centers is transparency , with these projects following a common pattern: “projects announced after permits are already secured, developers who don’t return calls, local officials who signed NDAs before their neighbors knew a project was being considered.” As a result of that backlash, New York announced a one-year moratorium on permits for large data centers , and according to Garman, there are more than 100 data center moratoriums currently being considered across the United States. “If these measures are enacted, the U.S. could be writing its own losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations,” Garman claimed. “As a country, we can’t afford to find ourselves in that position.” Garman also attempted to puncture what he said are four big myths around data centers: that they consume too much water, that they increase electricity costs, that they emit an enormous amount of pollution, and that they don’t provide any benefits to their communities. Pointing to an Amazon report about its own water usage , Garman said that “direct data center water consumption” only accounts for 0.5% of all industrial water usage in the United States, “orders of magnitude less than golf courses, almond farming, and many other industries.” Nvidia recently said its new cooling system eliminates “pretty much all water usage” inside the data center , but those claims — like Amazon’s — seem to ignore the broader water usage involved in electricity generation and chip manufacturing. Scientists have also said they need to study data centers’ water and energy usage independently , since there are no federal or state requirements around how tech companies report this data. As for electricity rates, Garman said they’ve only gone up in some states with large numbers of data centers, while they’ve gone down or at least grown more slowly in others. And he argued, “In instances where energy rates are going up, it’s primarily because the grid is old and hasn’t been invested in and expanded before the demand arrived.” On the other hand, an independent watchdog said recently data centers were the main culprit behind a 76% year-over-year price increase on America’s largest electrical grid. When it comes to pollution — an issue that the NAACP is currently suing Elon Musk’s SpaceX/xAI over — Garman complained that critics focus on the maximum amount of pollution allowed under data center permits. For example, a planned Amazon data center in Texas is permitted to release 33 million tons of carbon dioxide per year, which is more than any other power plant in the United States. “The truth is data center generators almost never run,” Garman said. “They’re idle 99.9% of the time (they run roughly 10 hours per year, mostly for required maintenance testing).”

articles.title: OpenAI safety employee resigns, claiming the company’s ‘culture is broken’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary: By his own admission, David Robinson is “something of a cliché”: an employee at a leading AI company who issues a dire warning while resigning from their job.
articles.body_text: By his own admission, David Robinson is “something of a cliché”: an employee at a leading AI company who issues a dire warning while resigning from their job. In an essay published in The Atlantic , Robinson said he led the writing of safety reports that accompanied OpenAI’s major product launches. He also said that with three-and-a-half years at OpenAI, he is “among the longest-tenured employees at the company.” Now he’s quitting, because in his view, the company’s “culture is broken.” In some ways, Robinson’s comments echo those of Jacob Coxon, who worked as a researcher at both OpenAI and Anthropic before quitting and declaring that these companies are “gambling with our lives.” Coxon’s comments led to a broader debate about AI safety, with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei unveiling a plan for more cautious AI development ; AI executives met with President Donald Trump this week and signed what appeared to be hastily written, non-binding pledge to implement more safety controls . But in Robinson’s view, the debate needs to go beyond “specific rules or new laws,” addressing the overall culture at these companies. And while much of the reporting around OpenAI has focused on how the company’s CEO Sam Altman lost the trust of former colleagues , Robinson’s essay suggests that OpenAI’s culture issues are the same as those of Silicon Valley at large. “OpenAI has thrived by trial and error (which it calls ‘iterative deployment’), looking for problems and improving its guardrails in response,” he wrote. “But this approach, by its very nature, guarantees periodic failures — and the scale of those failures is growing as systems get more capable.” Pointing to the recent breach of Hugging Face systems by OpenAI agents, as well as continuing revelations of OpenAI discovering more rogue agents , Robinson argued, “An environment where things like this can happen is no place to grow artificial minds that could be smarter than we are and that might not do what we want them to.” Given the increased risk, Robinson argued that frontier AI companies need to start operating “like nuclear-power plants or busy airports, with layers of redundancy and careful, time-consuming planning, so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster.” But Robinson said that in his time at OpenAI, he “never encountered a colleague who had experience making airplanes fly safely or nuclear reactors run without melting down, or helping the financial system grow without collapsing.” In response to Robinson’s essay, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company continues to improve its safety measures. “We’re making sure our models don’t become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down,” Pusateri said in a statement. “We’re making significant changes to strengthen security in our research and testing environments, train models to not just complete tasks but do so responsibly, expand our work with third-party evaluators, and improve real-time monitoring so we can detect and respond to concerning behavior earlier in the training process .” Beyond calling for changes in OpenAI’s culture, Robinson also said it’s time to ask bigger questions about alignment — something that he admitted could sound “touchy-feely,” but he said it’s critical as companies’ current “measures of how well” AI systems “match human values are coarse.” “The smarter the industry lets models grow while these problems remain unsolved, the more dangerous our situation becomes,” he said.

articles.title: Jack Dorsey's Bitchat disappears from app stores in India after government order | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Bitchat has become largely unavailable in India as a result of the restrictions.
articles.body_text: Bitchat, Jack Dorsey’s decentralized messaging app designed to work without an internet connection, has disappeared from Apple and Google’s app stores in India, months after New Delhi first sought to restrict access to the open-source software. Dorsey said Saturday that the Indian government had ordered Apple to remove Bitchat from its App Store in the country. In a notice from Apple that Dorsey posted on X, India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology issued the demand under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, the country’s primary legal provision for government-ordered online blocking. Apple’s notice said Bitchat would remain available on its App Store outside India. However, access to the app through its TestFlight beta-testing service would also be blocked in the country. Bitchat was also no longer available for download through Google Play in India when TechCrunch checked on Saturday. Bitchat’s website was also inaccessible across various internet service providers in the country. It was not immediately clear whether Google and internet service providers had also received directions from the federal government. Apple, Google, and India’s IT ministry did not respond to requests for comment. Launched in July last year, Bitchat uses Bluetooth mesh networking to allow nearby devices to exchange encrypted messages without relying on cellular networks, internet access, or centralized servers. In July 2026, Dorsey revealed that Indian authorities had ordered GitHub to take down repositories associated with the open-source messaging app, raising questions among digital rights advocates and legal experts about the legal basis for restricting software based on its functionality. The Internet Freedom Foundation, a New Delhi-based digital rights advocacy group, called the latest order unconstitutional, arguing that Section 69A allows the government to block unlawful information but not a messaging app because of its ability to operate during internet shutdowns. It also said neither the blocking order nor the allegedly illegal content cited as the basis for the action had been made public. The latest restrictions on Bitchat come as India is seeing a fresh wave of ⁠youth-led protests over changes to the country’s voter rolls.
